title: Sign-in, session lifecycle, logout and safe return navigation
permissions: Public sign-in; authenticated self-session operations
states: unknown→authenticated→expired/revoked; logout converges without a live session
validation: Zod login; normalized email; password verification; local safe redirect
failures: Invalid address/password uses one message; limiter refusal; expired rows removed; cookie/session creation can fail after account auth
Untrusted deployment forwarding headers can defeat IP attribution; concurrent check/record is not a hard reservation; limiter database errors are not independently recovered here.
decision: Preserve outcomes; replace custom session/password plumbing with Better Auth. Confirm freshness/re-auth policy explicitly; do not treat unused fresh metadata as implemented security.
behavior: Custom auth generates 20 random bytes encoded base32, stores SHA-256 session IDs, uses 30-day expiry with sliding refresh below 15 days. verifyFreshSession re-reads the session; it does not enforce the schema comment’s ten-minute fresh flag. Session metadata columns exist but normal login createsSession without IP/user-agent/geolocation. The production shared limiter counts only success=false auth_attempts newer than the strict sliding-window cutoff. Login permits fewer than 5 failures per normalized email and fewer than 20 per resolved IP in 15 minutes; at either threshold it refuses before lookup/password verification. recordAttempt writes/prunes older-than-24-hour rows in a batch, and success clears this identifier/kind’s failed rows within its window (also reducing that identifier’s contribution to its IP). REAL_ATTEMPT_LIMITER merely binds the same production counter/recorder for self-service injection; it is not a second limiter. getRequestIp prefers trimmed x-real-ip, otherwise the last x-forwarded-for hop, otherwise null; a null IP skips that axis. This relies on the deployment overwriting trusted proxy headers. Count/check and later record are separate, so concurrent attempts can exceed the nominal threshold. Request-boundary behavior is separately preserved by IDN-028.
acceptance: Correct/incorrect credentials, return-path attacks, expiry, revoke, repeated logout and credential rotation are exercised through real requests. Better Auth must provide equivalent renewal/revocation without relying on stale request-cached actors. Exercise identifier/IP isolation, normalized casing, exact window boundary, null IP, success cleanup without clearing other identifiers, and concurrent bursts using the real attempt store. Deployment tests prove a client cannot choose trusted IP headers; declare whether v3 limits failures, requests or both. IDN-028 covers cookie-presence versus validated-session routing and forged request headers.

title: Registration and account-entity provisioning
permissions: Public, constrained by invite/beta rules
states: account type planter/sending-church/network/discovery; invited seat/coach overrides ordinary standing
validation: Email/password/name/account type; required org name for relevant account types; unique email
failures: Existing-email error disclosed here; unique-email race caught; association redemption failures logged after account creation; registration/invitation revocation race accepted in v2
Failed-attempt policy is not a successful-registration volume cap; early validation/beta refusals can be uncounted; concurrent check and insert do not reserve a budget slot.
decision: Preserve all account types; redesign atomic grant and invitation redemption. No customer data migration.
behavior: Registration provisions orgs and their Owner or a preplant Owner; Discovery has an explicit profile and no seat. Invited planter may provision its plant immediately. Seat registration batches account and claim; org invitation redemption is a later best-effort operation. The accepted revoke race can leave an account with authority after the invite was revoked. Its shared register policy has a 1-hour window, 3 failures per IP and no identifier threshold. The action records duplicate-address/unique-conflict failures, records successful registration as success, and returns on malformed input/beta-gate/invitation refusals without uniformly recording them. Therefore this source does not enforce a maximum of 3 successful registrations per IP/hour despite the policy comment’s mass-account-creation intent. Success also clears in-window register failures for that identifier; no-IP requests skip the sole axis.
acceptance: Each type provisions only intended entities. Revoke/expire racing registration yields either a valid complete grant or no grant; no orphan authority. Failure between account creation and relationship redemption has a retryable reconciliation receipt. Prove policy against real successful, duplicate, beta-refused, malformed and concurrent registrations; resolve the intended account-creation/request-volume cap before relying on library defaults. Null/untrusted IP behavior is covered by IDN-001.

title: Beta gate and meaningful invitation-origin registration
permissions: Public; bypass only valid addressed invitation
states: gate disabled/enabled; code absent/invalid/valid; open invitation addressed/unaddressed
validation: Email and pending unexpired invitation; account-type relationship
failures: Forged invitation does not bypass; invalid code field error; linked invitation can expire during form review
decision: Preserve optional controlled rollout; decide whether alpha beta-code gate is needed in fresh v3 before activation.
behavior: Registration has separate account-type choice policy and beta invitation bypass. Invitation information must describe inviter sufficiently for informed consent without exposing target account existence to senders.
acceptance: Bypass matrix covers unrelated email, expired/revoked invite, each account type and disabled gate. Public response contains no secret gate value.

title: Development and managed-preview account switching
permissions: Public only under development/owned-preview flag
states: disabled→unreachable; enabled→fixture selection→session
validation: Allowlisted fixture account; explicit environment guard
failures: Refuse outside selected environment; no user-submitted arbitrary privilege
decision: Keep isolated developer tooling; require fresh v3 fixture accounts, never clone customers or enable in production.
behavior: Hidden login helpers support reproducible persona/role UI checks. They are not a production identity feature. Preview account catalog and role matrix are evidence assets.
acceptance: Production build with flags absent cannot obtain a fixture session via forged action POST. Owned test environment can switch only seeded personas.

title: Seat, tenancy, capability guards and read-only affordances
permissions: Owner/Admin/Member scoped to exactly one tenancy; coach assignments separate
states: seated/seatless/discovery/misprovisioned; multiple-tenancy rows fail closed
validation: Tenancy plus seat, not seat alone; operation-specific own-duty subject guard
failures: Stale actors; two tenancy FKs; hidden control is not server authorization; canAccessFeatureData is consent only and does not prove church reach
decision: Keep flat role policy and real isolation. Simplify source-text capability drift tests into runtime permission contracts; do not build a configurable per-module permission grid.
behavior: Flat seats: Owner relationship/privacy/seat changes; Admin ordinary writes; Member reads and own-duty writes. Org seats read aggregates, never individual CRM. Coach is read-only by assignment. General access helper returns org reach first, otherwise plant seat or assignment reach; scoped coaching readers explicitly check assignments, so an org-seated coach can read assigned plants through coaching routes. Schema users lacks exactly-one-tenancy and seat-tenancy CHECKs because historical rows were tolerated.
acceptance: Role×tenancy×operation and foreign-ID matrices are executable contracts. Explicit grant contexts distinguish own seat, assigned coach read, oversight aggregate. Malformed membership cannot widen read/write; clients cannot forge capability arrays.

title: Account avatar upload, replacement, removal and authenticated delivery
permissions: Authenticated self only
states: no avatar→uploaded→replaced/removed
validation: JPG/JPEG/PNG/WebP; nonempty; max 3 MiB; generated key
failures: Upload before row; write before old-object delete; cleanup failure logged; upload followed by failed write may orphan new object
decision: Preserve private delivery/order; share upload policy/storage adapter with person photos, use cleanup jobs rather than generic event infrastructure.
behavior: users.avatar_key stores a private key. Browser receives session-gated route with version segment, never a raw storage key or signed photo URL. Account name is displayed but no account-name mutation exists in the audited account action file.
acceptance: Unauthorized route 401; user A cannot request user B avatar by arbitrary key; changed photo visible despite browser cache; failed deletion keeps new photo usable; failed write retains old photo.

title: Email change request, proof, confirmation and security notice
permissions: Authenticated own account and current password
states: new request supersedes live request; pending→consumed or expired; duplicate new address refuses swap
validation: Normalized valid address; different address; current password; token hash; unique login email
failures: Provider failure surfaced as emailSent; superseded/wrong-account/dead links refused; unique address collision; main raw Date predicates have host-zone risk repaired in alpha
decision: Keep safety semantics via Better Auth or thin domain adapter; implement credential-operation concurrency and explicit CRM email policy, avoiding duplicate auth workflows.
behavior: Confirmation is mailbox proof for changing login identifier, not initial-registration email verification. Alpha locks account and checks current email/password snapshots, fixes timestamp predicates, invalidates password-reset requests after confirmed change. Main does not synchronize the CRM contact email with new login email. The shared email_change policy uses the authenticated account’s current normalized email, not the target address: 3 outstanding/failed attempts per identifier and 10 per IP in 1 hour. Wrong current password and valid unconfirmed requests are recorded false; successful confirmation records true for the previous login identifier and clears its in-window failures. Malformed/same-address refusals do not record an attempt. The settings adapter obtains actor from requireSeat("self.write"); token confirmation verifies request.userId equals that actor, and SQL swaps only that actor’s row/current email. A request-supplied user ID cannot select the account.
acceptance: Expired/superseded links and concurrent password reset/change cannot resurrect credentials. Confirmation takes effect exactly once and preserves account/person identity; storage timestamps round-trip under non-UTC process zone. Vary target mailboxes without evading the own-account threshold; malformed and wrong-secret cases match the chosen policy. Forged account IDs/tokens for another user cannot confirm or change the actor; successful confirmation clears only the previous identifier/kind budget.

title: Authenticated password change and other-session revocation
permissions: Authenticated self with current password
states: unchanged/refused; new hash committed; other sessions ended; current session retained
validation: At least 8 characters; current secret; disallow identical password; throttle before expensive hash
failures: Main writes hash without stale-snapshot compare; alpha locks user and validates email/hash snapshot, conditionally revokes other sessions and outstanding reset/email tokens
decision: Preserve behavior; adopt Better Auth, verify its revocation and reset-token invalidation rather than assuming plugin defaults suffice.
behavior: Password change counts own current-email failures and returns number of other sessions ended. Alpha adds credential-race protection; password_reset_requests is alpha-only. Its shared password_change policy is separate from login counts but has the same 15-minute window, 5 failures per own current-email identifier and 20 per IP. Wrong current password records false; a successful change records true and clears that identifier/kind; short/unchanged-password refusals do not record. The server adapter obtains user and currentSessionId from requireSeat("self.write"), never input. Hash update is scoped to actor.id; session deletion is scoped to sessions.userId=actor.id AND session.id!=currentSessionId. Alpha adds locked email/hash snapshot predicates around that scope.
acceptance: Two stale tabs, reset/change/email-change races preserve only winning credentials; current session remains if requested, other sessions invalidated immediately. Wrong current password cannot test new-secret equivalence. Exercise password-change budget independently of login, at both identifier/IP thresholds and with null IP. A forged currentSessionId or actor ID in JSON cannot spare another account’s session or update another user; only the actual authenticated session survives. Verify the chosen treatment of malformed/unchanged new passwords.

title: Mailbox password recovery
permissions: Public generic request; expiring mailbox capability authorizes reset
states: request→superseded/expired/consumed; reset→all sessions revoked
validation: 64 lowercase hex token; 1-hour expiry; 8–1024 char password; confirmation match; email/password snapshot
failures: Generic response even absent account/mail failure; stale or reused token refused; DB errors swallowed on request; reset success survives notice failure
decision: Include in full target and early identity slice; use Better Auth recovery after proving equivalent concurrency and no-enumeration semantics.
behavior: Verified only at alpha2107df58, absent main. One live request/account, hashed token, transaction locks and snapshot predicates revoke every session plus pending email/reset requests on success. No automatic signed-in session after reset. Alpha adds password_reset to the shared limiter: 1 hour, 3 requests per normalized requested email and 10 per IP. A syntactically mailable request records false before account lookup, so missing/existing accounts consume the same budget and return the same generic response. Invalid addresses bypass lookup/record. Successful reset records true and clears that identifier/kind’s window. Recovery authority comes from the hashed, live, unconsumed token bound to its request/user plus email/password snapshots; no session actor or client-supplied account ID is accepted.
acceptance: Replay, concurrent redemption, changed email/hash, non-UTC process, provider outage and all-session revocation pass. Request latency/output does not expose account existence. Existing/nonexistent addresses consume equal budgets, threshold refusals remain generic, and expired/foreign/purpose-mismatched tokens cannot select another user. Assert token-derived account/session/token invalidation predicates and concurrency with credential changes against disposable PostgreSQL.

title: Settings modal, deep links, draft protection and section API
permissions: Section visibility/read from server actor; account/notifications all accounts; church Admin+; team Admin+; association subject Owner/discovery
states: closed/open; idle/draft/dirty/saving/error; deprecated sharing→church
validation: Known section IDs; safe default; source-owned authorization per section
failures: Blocked navigation/dismissal while dirty; forbidden section withheld; fetch/cache refresh/stale draft risks
decision: Keep settings capabilities and draft safety. Compare modal with simple route UI during design; changing shell is allowed, losing deep links or drafts is not.
behavior: Hash modal preserves current workspace. Legacy settings routes redirect to dashboard hash. Server supplies typed section DTOs; preferences autosave, account/church edits have explicit drafts. Re-evaluate modal complexity as UX choice, not immutable architecture.
acceptance: Deep link/back/forward, Escape, focus trap/restore, dirty switching and server refusal work across personas; rejected save retains draft; cached settings never show another account’s state.

title: Church profile, locality, timezone, inactivity and digest schedule
permissions: Plant Owner/Admin; sharing remains Owner only
states: profile fields editable; local-zone/schedule effective after save
validation: Field lengths/name required; IANA zone; weekday0–6/hour0–23; warning/alert1–365 with warning<alert
failures: Invalid zone/schedule refused; changing zone must not reinterpret legacy meeting wall-clock storage; raw UTC calendar conversions
decision: Preserve fields/preferences; standardize LocalDate, Instant, ZonedSchedule. Avoid address-based inferred timezone or redundant launch-date church column.
behavior: Plant name, street, city, region, country independently editable. Default America/Chicago; digest Sunday16:00. Street excluded from oversight. Date-only meeting/task/commitment semantics need a unified v3 date contract.
acceptance: Each field can be cleared where nullable. Invalid thresholds/schedule fail before write and at DB where arithmetic. DST transitions and zone change produce intended local scheduled delivery and badges.

supporting_evidence_notes.role: shared operational support, not independent capability/public API

title: Per-account notification preferences, cadence and self suppression recovery
permissions: Authenticated self; org preferences cannot widen church consent
states: per category/channel on/off; daily/weekly cadence; suppressed→self cleared
validation: Closed categories/channels/cadences; caller’s current email
failures: Saving failure must restore UI; clearing suppression is not consent to unrelated email; caller cannot clear another address
decision: Retain settings and integrate with notification-owned contracts; no parallel preference engine.
behavior: Audience-specific preference matrix differs for plant and oversight users. Suppression state reported and self-clear control exists. Execution/notification pipeline owned in ops/communication audit; this record preserves settings entry points.
acceptance: User A preference changes never affect B; unsupported audience category refused; consent gate still applies despite enabled org push preference; self-clear affects only own current address.

title: Church creation, onboarding basics and account-person bootstrap
permissions: Church-level preplant Owner; discovery uses separate conversion
states: uncreated→created; duplicate request→existing plant; lost link→best-effort discard
validation: Required trimmed name; optional independent locality parts
failures: Main batched create can lose link race and leave disposable orphan before cleanup; no DB work should use shared production-like branch for proofs
decision: Preserve flow; use one true transaction with locked account/unique membership and idempotency key. Do not carry compensate-after-commit as required design.
behavior: Creates plant, links Owner, adds all-off privacy and account-linked Person in one batch. Basics step becomes nonreenterable after success. Initial current_phase0 is default, not attestation. New v3 bootstrap initializes canonical global data independently from this customer-facing operation.
acceptance: Double submit produces one owned plant; failed creation leaves no orphan authority/people/settings; locality can be partly supplied; default phase is visibly unattested.

title: Leadership attestation, vacant-owner claim and prompts
permissions: Current Owner or Member when plant has no Owner; Admin explicitly excluded
states: unanswered/legacy owner-inferred; planter_confirmed/no_planter; confirm/claim/decline
validation: yes/no; same church; unique Owner indexes
failures: Concurrent claims one winner; no planter means some follow-up/evaluation tasks/owner notifications cannot be created; legacy unknown differs from no
decision: Preserve attestation/claim; explicitly resolve Owner versus lead-pastor modeling before schema freeze. Do not let Evry appoint pastoral authority.
behavior: Leadership answer and actual Owner assignment are distinct. Owner may declare no_planter yet retain owner authority; role labels and pastoral responsibility must be shown consistently. Claim is a grant operation, not ordinary write capability.
acceptance: Racing Members cannot both become Owner; Admin cannot claim; no_planter and unanswered render distinct prompts; missing recipients produce observable deferred work rather than silent task loss.

source_wrapper_aliases.role: source controller wrapper/side-effect chain; not a required public v3 API

title: Journey declaration, launch-date setup, completion and resume
permissions: Church-level Owner; declaration distinct from later phase transition
states: basics→leadership→journey→people→finish; optional steps skippable; persisted missing-facts resume
validation: Known journey stages; not_sure→phase0 attestation; launch date owned by launches; existing date cannot be removed by setup
failures: Launch schedule can succeed before initial-phase declaration fails; repeat must converge; browser history after first step and finish must not reopen invalid state
decision: Keep journey and human judgment; consolidate typed domain orchestration rather than calling one Next server action from another.
behavior: Four steps; completion sets onboarding_completed_at independent of all facts being filled. Incomplete indicator surfaces missing facts later. Initial phase is planter attestation and never automated judgment; launch plan accepts no-date and cannot clear existing schedule during onboarding. Completion uses IS NULL and atomically stamps last_material_event_at for later scheduled Plant Intelligence; it does not synchronously generate an assessment.
acceptance: All skip/resume/back/finish routes follow persisted facts; initial attestation is exactly once; partial launch/phase save is recoverable; v3 no data migration/backfill.

title: Discovery identity, associations and conversion to plant
permissions: Explicit own Discovery profile; org Owner may sever own discovery association
states: unassociated/associated discovery→plant Owner; associated discovery must leave before first seat
validation: No seat/tenant; fresh profile/account lock; preserve association and disclosed sharing choice on plant conversion
failures: Racing first seat/conversion/association must not create competing identity; retained coach assignments unaffected
decision: Preserve distinct exploration identity; model lifecycle explicitly with atomic conversion, not a broad null-FK fallback.
behavior: Row existence defines Discovery, never inference from tenancy absence. Can associate with sending church/network without org seat. Conversion carries chosen org links, retires profile and audits transfer; consent is explicit in conversion UI. Seatless former Member is not automatically Discovery.
acceptance: Foreign profile reads denied; conversion versus association/seat acceptance race has one consistent result; leave association allows first seat; coaching survives conversion without granting writes elsewhere.

title: Seat invitation create, pending list, resend, revoke, expire and first-seat acceptance
permissions: Owner/Admin invites Admin/Member into own plant/sending church/network; token bound to invitee address; Owner never invitable
states: pending→accepted/expired/revoked; resend rotates token; existing seatless account may gain first seat
validation: Exactly one tenancy; seat kind has non-null admin/member; 30-day expiry; sha256 token; addressed live token; limiter
failures: Sender results must not expose account existence; refuse tenancy moves/associated discovery; concurrent resends supersede old token; v2 cooldown not globally reliable
decision: Preserve full lifecycle; choose dedicated MembershipInvitation domain despite Better Auth organization plugin, because association and coach grants remain different.
behavior: Signed-in acceptance supports existing seatless accounts and keeps coaching. Registration path separate from signed-in guarded INSERT/UPDATE claims. Settings listing redacts sensitive internal resolution data. Expiry is performed when loading settings, not solely a scheduler.
acceptance: All tenancy types, new/existing account, wrong-address, already seated, associated Discovery, concurrent revoke/accept/resend and duplicate request cases. Pending list/email action never leaks whether recipient has account.

title: Coach invitation and assignment lifecycle
permissions: Plant Owner/Admin invites/ends; any addressed authenticated account accepts; assignment grants read only
states: pending→accepted/revoked/expired; assignment active→inactive/reactivated
validation: Coach kind no seat; plant target; user+church unique assignment; no tenancy move
failures: Any Admin may end assignment despite FRD creator-Admin wording because assigned_by absent; cannot duplicate active grant; ended assignment immediately loses read
decision: Keep explicit grants; add assigned_by/end actor/date audit in fresh v3, decide whether creator-specific end authority is product-needed.
behavior: Coaches may also hold a separate tenancy seat. Acceptance changes no seat/tenant and mints no person row in coached plant. Main and alpha carry author-provenance limitation.
acceptance: Org Member, plant Member, coach-only account can accept without gaining plant writes; revoke assignment removes every scoped read; repeated invite cannot duplicate grant.

title: Seat roster, Admin appointment/demotion and authority removal
permissions: Own tenancy Owner changes Member/Admin; cannot remove own/Owner seat
states: Member↔Admin; seated→seatless; coach grants independent
validation: Same tenancy; expected prior role; target UUID; explicit remove confirmation
failures: Racing role changes/refused stale target; main task effect includes noncomplete tasks, alpha actionable statuses only; CRM and memberships preserved
decision: Preserve authority removal/reconciliation; stamp grants and changes in audit. Adopt membership table while retaining one-current-seat product rule unless separately approved.
behavior: Joined date uses accepted invite or account created fallback. Removal revokes sessions, clears tenancy/seat, assigns unfinished duties to removing Owner and clears access-dependent team leader. Retains Person.user_id history, contact and ordinary team membership; removal is not ownership transfer or account deletion.
acceptance: Owner protection, foreign targets, two removals and race with leadership appointment. Person/assessment/team history survives; released duties reassignable; alpha terminal waived/cancelled tasks not reopened or reassigned as outstanding.

title: Organization relationship invitations across five subject types
permissions: Org Owner creates; plant Owner/sending-church Owner/own Discovery answer their addressed subject; org Admin/Member read only
states: pending→accepted/declined/expired/revoked; first-association defaults only on accepted claim
validation: Five type/target variants; normalized mailable email; UUIDs; 30-day window;3 invites/address/window; no duplicate pending; slot cannot silently replace association
failures: Concurrent competing accepts/revoke guarded with target lock; mail failure cannot undo invite; sender redaction; nullable expiry historical rows; no persisted delivery status
decision: Retain every relationship variant. Split focused invitation policy, transaction repository and delivery adapter; no generic nullable subject mega-service.
behavior: Organization association is not account seating. Plant may relate independently to sending church/network; sending-church to network; Discovery to either. Invitation core is a large mixed policy/persistence/mail module; typed discriminated subjects make most SQL variant boilerplate avoidable.
acceptance: Each variant can create/read/answer/resend/revoke with scoped actors; competing associations never replace consent; inviter description meaningful; no sender account enumeration; email retry preserves one invitation.

title: Relationship leaving, organization severing and association history
permissions: Subject Owner/own Discovery may leave; org Owner severs own relationship; deliberate confirmation
states: associated→disassociated; append-only associated/disassociated events; rejoin keeps prior consent
validation: Exactly one event subject; matching org reach; confirmation strings validated in actions
failures: Notification failure logged after committed sever; sending-church subject history written but omitted by existing plant-filter reader; imported legacy relationships have no invented audit
decision: Preserve lifecycle/history; make relationship transaction plus delivery outbox atomic, implement subject-aware history UI.
behavior: Audit records actor/org/subject/source invite/time. Ending association is not delete or seat move. History is private/scoped and cannot reconstruct arbitrary church feature toggle. Direct legacy sever helpers are inventoried separately as unused.
acceptance: Both sides sever exactly their own link, repeated sever benign/no-new event, opposite side notified retryably; history shows all three subject kinds in v3 without inventing missing provenance.

title: Privacy pull sharing, push consent and first-invitation defaults
permissions: Plant Owner controls disclosure; oversight read is additionally relationship scoped
states: all-off self-start; disclosed first invite enables defaults; later associations preserve choices; off sends coarse notice
validation: Known feature keys/boolean; one settings row/church; updated_by; pull distinct from activity push
failures: Missing settings fails closed; main rejoining after last org can reset consent, alpha guards accepted invites/audit; finance/facility toggles persist without active modules
decision: Preserve actual consent needs; decide granularity/defaults openly. Remove dead toggle from v3 schema only through explicit decision; do not resurrect facilities simply because column exists.
behavior: Current active aggregates: People/Meetings/Tasks/Teams/Wiki, plus activity push. Financials deferred; facilities removed direction but schema/toggle still present. Invite defaults are shared plant-wide, not per-org; changing any off emits coarse consent-exempt notice without naming toggle.
acceptance: Rejoin and simultaneous different org association never overwrite existing choices. Sharing-off does not remove relationship listing. Org notification preference cannot authorize private pull. No individual CRM through oversight, even sharePeople on.

title: Oversight dashboard, plant directory, consent-gated aggregates and health entry
permissions: Own org Owner/Admin/Member aggregate reads only
states: relationship listed regardless sharing; section withheld/shared-empty/shared-populated
validation: Org reach before consent; person totals never identify individuals; locality excludes street
failures: Unknown/foreign church indistinguishable; empty differs withheld; alpha task open/overdue excludes cancelled/waived; UTC date counting needs church-local contract
decision: Keep aggregate-only oversight; shared domain reporting queries prevent parallel inconsistent counts. Phase owner must finalize health consent contract.
behavior: Directory name/locality/planter/phase/launch/provenance is relationship context. Feature sections contain totals, status distribution, meeting recent12 cadence/attendance, task status/overdue, teams/leader coverage, wiki reading totals. /oversight/health delegates to Phase Engine owner; do not confuse section share settings with intelligence data-consent rail.
acceptance: Sharing matrix includes each aggregate and empty/withheld copy; network never inherits private person DTO; task checklist/terminal semantics agree with domain totals; launch countdown evaluated in intentional date zone.

title: Network sending-church roster and member detail
permissions: Network seats read; sending-church seats cannot enumerate network roster
states: no members/roster; member with plant/pending counts
validation: Own network FK; UUID; plant requires sending church AND same network; pending expiry
failures: Foreign/unknown member null; counts must not include outside-network plants; no hierarchy walk grants access
decision: Preserve dedicated scoped reporting, avoid generic graph hierarchy authorization.
behavior: Roster summarizes associated sending churches and pending invitations; member detail lists only same-network plants, links to existing aggregate-only plant route. Empty states are explanatory.
acceptance: Network A cannot list/detail B; sending-church user rejected; inactive/expired pending invitations excluded; link targets still honor per-plant consent.

title: Coach plant, collection and detail surfaces
permissions: Active own assignment; read only independent of oversight sharing; separate seat lends no write
states: 25-row paged collections; assignment active/inactive; unknown→not found
validation: UUIDs; closed collection names; bounded positive page; tenant joins; deleted records excluded
failures: FRD promises full People assessments/interviews/commitments, implemented coached people DTO omits them; no scoped photo route/communication/activity UI in audited coach surface
decision: Preserve implemented read surfaces and close promised omissions. Confirm scope of communications/activity, assessments and private documents with product owner; no silent downgrade.
behavior: Actual coached record details include contacts/address/background-check/tags/skills; task steps; meeting attendance/evaluation; team roles/roster. It is not full parity with plant’s own records. No write controls. Own-seat plus assignment can coexist; explicit grant context avoids accidental mixing.
acceptance: Inactive/wrong assignment, foreign records and malformed pages disclose nothing. Full People qualification/history/document reads required by FRD are designed as explicit coach read operations; sensitive photo/document access follows grant.

title: Unwired organization settings, ownership transfer and account deletion boundaries
permissions: org.settings Owner-only declared; transfer/delete not implemented
states: capability declared but no route; ownership transfer/delete deferred
validation: No existing API contract to reuse
failures: Do not mistake removing seat for deleting CRM or transferring ownership
decision: Explicit decision required; preserve boundary and expose gap. Do not count future billing/transfer as implemented.
behavior: org.settings exists only as policy declaration. Settings has account/church/team/association/notifications, no org profile/billing authoring. Church deletion through support; transfer needs own audit/notification design. These are documented nonimplemented directions, not full implemented capabilities.
acceptance: Complete target accounts for org profile/transfer/delete as open explicit product decisions. Until approved, no UI/tool can transfer/delete underlying tenancy merely by removing a seat.

title: Unused direct disassociation helpers
permissions: No actor parameter; no callers found in src
states: direct FK→null without audit
validation: Identifier only; no public guarded route
failures: Would bypass authorization/audit if used as service surface
decision: Replace/remove internal dead helpers as implementation cleanup; preserve actual sever capability IDN-021.
behavior: Static search found each name only at its exported definition, with no src caller. Their exports exist but are not implemented product flows. Audited sever operations with receipt/audit remain the authoritative behavior.
acceptance: V3 exposes only audited actor-bearing sever operations; no unguarded direct-FK helper becomes an Evry tool.

title: Request boundary, CSRF exceptions, trusted routing and expired-session recovery
permissions: Cookie presence is an early routing hint only; a validated session/current domain grant authorizes private routes and operations.
Public preview is limited to the real routed Wiki path and deliberately public content; a user-agent or client header never grants private authority.
CSRF-exempt writes derive authority exclusively from the verified provider signature or sealed disable-only unsubscribe token, never ambient sessions.
states: no cookie protected GET → safe local login return path
cookie present + invalid/expired/revoked session → layout login redirect → reachable login form
valid session → authenticated shell; login page bounces only after session validation
real allowlisted Wiki path + crawler UA + no user → metadata shell only
non-GET missing/malformed/cross-host Origin → 403 unless exact self-authenticating exception
validation: All continued requests overwrite x-routed-url with actual pathname+search; layout derives route scope from that stamped value and UA, never x-is-crawler.

Current proxy compares parsed Origin.host to Host; scheme is not compared. Missing Origin/Host refuses, including HEAD/OPTIONS in this matched path policy. Forwarded/Host trust is a deployment assumption to verify.
Exact CSRF exceptions only /api/webhooks/resend and /api/notifications/unsubscribe; lookalike child paths and other machine APIs are not exempt.
Safe return path rejects non-relative/external, protocol-relative, leading slash-backslash and control-character values, preserving valid query paths.
integrations: Next proxy request-header override and dashboard layout
Better Auth replacement must retain outcome without copying Next-specific middleware
Resend raw-body Svix signature verifier (communications owner)
Sealed unsubscribe capability and confirmation/undo (notifications owner)
failures: Expired cookie can be renewed at proxy without a live DB session; keeping /login reachable prevents the historical redirect loop.
Changing crawler allowlist or trusting a client-supplied routed URL could bypass the intended shell boundary; current header overwrite and shared predicate prevent this.
Host-only Origin comparison is narrower than full scheme/host/port same-origin validation; separate backend/reverse-proxy topology requires an explicit tested policy.
Originless signed job/API callers outside the exact two exceptions currently receive 403; do not broaden the bypass to accommodate them without defining self-authentication.
The webhook route evidence includes import-graph tests rather than full signature/failure integration; v3 must add request-level adversarial tests.
decision: Preserve secure outcomes and recoverable navigation. Choose backend/CORS/proxy deployment policy explicitly; do not preserve cookie-presence authentication, host-only comparison or internal routing headers as architectural dogma. Wiki preview content and email capability semantics are owned by their module specs.
behavior: The proxy performs early GET routing on cookie presence for /, /register, /dashboard, /oversight and the Wiki preview prefixes. It deliberately leaves /login reachable; the login page validates the session before redirecting, and the dashboard layout validates the session for the entire authenticated group including routes absent from the proxy prefix list. Every continued request overwrites x-routed-url with actual pathname+query. Layout re-derives crawler scope from UA and that trusted route stamp; x-is-crawler is ignored and never emitted. Forging a crawler UA can reach only the deliberately previewable real Wiki path, not People/settings/other private routes. GET cookie renewal (30 days, HttpOnly, SameSite Lax, Secure in production) is not session validity. Every matched non-GET request requires Origin and Host with parsed host equality, except the two exact independently authenticated routes. Resend verifies the raw body against Svix headers/secret. Unsubscribe GET redirects to a confirmation page without writing; POST derives only user/category from its sealed disable-only token and changes only that email preference, with uniform invalid-token 200 behavior. The one-click body marker is diagnostic, not authority. Normal confirmation/undo server actions remain under the ordinary origin guard; enable-only undo uses a separately purposed short-lived token. Detailed public Wiki and email workflows remain with communications/notifications owners.
acceptance: Issue real requests with no cookie, forged cookie, expired/deleted/revoked session and a valid session for every authenticated route family; stale-cookie login must render without loops and preserve safe path/query. Forge x-routed-url=/wiki and x-is-crawler with ordinary/crawler UAs on People/settings/tasks/teams/meetings/notifications/dashboard/oversight: private data stays unavailable, and the internal route stamp always reflects actual URL. A genuine Wiki preview returns only its approved public projection. Test missing/malformed Origin, cross-host, same-host different scheme/port, HEAD/OPTIONS/CORS preflight and deployment Host/forwarded-header handling against the declared v3 policy. Exact originless webhook/unsubscribe requests work only with valid signature/sealed token; forged/expired/wrong-purpose tokens or signatures never mutate. Unsubscribe GET stays read-only, POST cannot enable email or change another category/account, and originless lookalike/dispatch/revalidate paths receive the declared refusal. Test source-backed safe-return attacks including protocol-relative/backslash/control characters and valid nested query paths. Domain action/API authority is checked again after route admission; private access cannot rely on proxy or UI checks.

title: People directory, search, filters, cursor pagination and views
permissions: Own plant seated readers; mutations separate; oversight never directory
states: list/card/pipeline view; filter/bookmark→paged results
validation: Closed status/source; canonical UUID tag IDs; all-selected-tags AND; bounded1–100 limit;24-page UI
failures: Foreign/invalid cursor ignored; equal createdAt uses ID tie-break; search SQL wildcards not escaped unlike duplicate matcher; entire pipeline loads all contacts
decision: Preserve read affordances; one typed query DTO reused by UI, exports and Evry; use scalable pipeline pagination/virtualization without changing stages.
behavior: Directory search includes full name/email/phone; status/source/tag filters retained in URL and load-more. Soft-deleted excluded by default. No high test count substitutes for browser/filter interaction proofs.
acceptance: Changing each filter/search/view resets pagination while preserving siblings; equal-time rows neither duplicate nor vanish; foreign cursor cannot disclose data; inactive badges use church-local policy.

title: Person creation, quick add, profile editing and background-check tracking
permissions: Plant Owner/Admin; Member/coach read only
states: new prospect or selected status; background not_started/in_progress/cleared/flagged
validation: Required first/last max255; optional email/phone/address/source; status enum; background DB CHECK
failures: Zod min before trim can accept whitespace-only name; form blank→undefined prevents clearing some fields; update emits no generic person_updated activity; separate event/history writes partial
decision: Preserve manual background tracking and all fields. Boundary DTOs should allow explicit null and trimmed validation; screening provider remains separate unapproved scope.
behavior: Fields include contact/address/source/sourceDetails/notes/background status; manual tracking only, no screening-provider integration. Quick add defaults prospect/US/source other. UserId and storage keys stripped at client boundary.
acceptance: Whitespace-only names rejected; nullable contact fields clear explicitly; immutable account link cannot be supplied; all profile changes have actor/version audit; flagged is never automatically treated cleared.

title: Person retirement and service-only restore
permissions: Delete Owner/Admin; restore exported service lacks action/UI
states: active→soft-deleted→restored at service level; merged source retired separately
validation: Same church; restore requires deleted person; preserve references
failures: Soft deletion does not reconcile all assigned duties; merged sources could be restored by raw restore service despite merge semantics; deleted household FK retained
decision: Retain soft retirement/recovery requirement; implement safe operator/user restore only with product-approved policy, never hard-delete history.
behavior: Actual delete is deleted_at, preserving all CRM relational history and storage. Source search found restorePerson only definition; no delivered restore workflow. Retired merge redirects resolve to survivor.
acceptance: Full target defines recovery action and audited restore, excluding merged sources or requiring explicit merge reversal review. Deleted records hidden from active queries yet history/receipts retained.

title: Account-linked contacts and recruited-contact identity
permissions: Account link conveys addressability, never permission; plant grant only mints/links
states: unlinked contact→linked account; seat removal retains link/history
validation: Unique church+user partial index; same email/active/unlinked rechecked; one-word name keeps empty last name
failures: Email-based fallback helper plus explicit userId can diverge after email change; ambiguous email picks oldest match; concurrent link races protected by index
decision: Keep separate human contact and account identity. Use explicit contact-account link exclusively for authority-related matching; decide email fallback compatibility with fresh data and duplicate-review UX.
behavior: Auto Owner Person at church creation is leader status; invited seat attempts oldest active same-email contact before minting account-linked person. Coach acceptance mints no contact. Recruited-contact exclusion prevents staff fixture/owner records inflating planting metrics. DTO strips userId/storage key but keeps operational person fields.
acceptance: Each church gain creates exactly one contact; same-email duplicates do not steal account authority; changed email/removed seat preserves intended recruited-contact classification; no client assignment writes userId.

title: Private person photo lifecycle
permissions: Plant Owner/Admin upload; own-plant authenticated read; coached photo not supplied by implemented route
states: none/upload/replacement/removal; merge chooses stored side
validation: Same3 MiB image policy; generated key; live same-plant person
failures: Delete old blob only after saved reference; failure cleanup logged; chosen merge photo may share retained source object; no public raw key
decision: Rename v3 column photoObjectId/key; retain secure delivery and ordering, shared storage adapter.
behavior: persons.photo_url misleadingly stores storage key. Client DTO replaces with session route/version. Merge picks stored row value, never user-provided object key.
acceptance: Foreign/deleted person photo404; no keys/raw signed URL in client; upload replacement visible; garbage cleanup never deletes referenced source/survivor blob; approved coach read protected by assignment.

title: Manual recruitment-stage movement, warnings, reasons and handoff
permissions: Owner/Admin; warnings are soft, server does not hard-gate methodology
states: prospect→attendee→following_up→interviewed→core_group→launch_team→leader; backwards/skips permitted
validation: Closed status; optional reason; active same-plant person
failures: Main profile-edit status bypasses warning flow; no optimistic version update; activity/event writes after status can fail; leaving committed set returns handoff proposal
decision: Keep authoritative status methodology; decide auto-regression behavior explicitly. Use atomic stage+audit and version precondition; Evry proposes stage changes for reviewed human writes.
behavior: Preserve all7 statuses and human override. Soft ordering reflects playbook, not a hard eligibility gate. Skips show warnings and skipped statuses; backwards confirmation UI; server accepts valid status. Same status no-op.
acceptance: Skipped/backward/manual status keeps reason/actor; concurrent edits cannot lose audit; moving from committed set presents/executes explicit duty handoff; no mandatory new theological gate.

title: Recruitment pipeline grouping, ordering, inactivity and follow-up warnings
permissions: All plant seats read; drag/reorder/status write Owner/Admin
states: 5 columns; final core_group column includes launch_team/leader milestone badges
validation: Ordered person IDs scoped to plant; empty reorder no-op; active parent follow-up statuses only
failures: No optimistic reorder version; loads all contacts; alpha active follow-up overdue/missing indicators absent main; cancelled/waived excluded in alpha
decision: Preserve board and warning enhancement; avoid exposing giant raw row graph to client, use paged cards with stable stage ordering.
behavior: Five columns deliberately coexist with seven statuses. Alpha adds actionable parent follow-up tasks to each card and overdue/no-follow-up warnings. This record is main grouping with alpha enhancement, not separate lost feature.
acceptance: Five-column grouping/badges exact; read-only no drag targets; reorder foreign IDs harmless/refused; missing/overdue follow-up uses due-date church-local boundary and terminal-state exclusion.

title: Activity timeline and authored-note create/edit/delete
permissions: Plant reads; Owner/Admin write notes; edit/delete only original author
states: note create→edited metadata; deleted note hard-removed; chronological activity
validation: Nonblank note; church+ID+note kind+author predicate
failures: Date-only cursor excludes tied timestamps and pops extra row cursor, risking skipped timeline entries; edit/delete personId ignored after note predicate; delete has no note revision history
decision: Preserve notes and history; separate mutable note content/revisions from immutable activity/audit rather than adopting unconstrained polymorphic Note blindly.
behavior: Timeline stores typed activity plus JSON metadata and performer display. Edit preserves timestamp, sets editedAt. Note is stored as activity metadata while persons.notes is separate summary field; per-feature notes are duplicated elsewhere.
acceptance: Equal-time activities fully paginate via composite cursor; authorship and exact person association checked; note edits/deletes preserve accountable revision/tombstone policy; ordinary audit entries never user-editable.

title: Household lifecycle, member roles and deliberate address propagation
permissions: Owner/Admin writes; own-plant reads
states: ungrouped→head/spouse/child/other; joined/left/role changed; household delete only empty active roster
validation: Same-plant active person and household; required name; optional address; role enum
failures: Accepted READ COMMITTED create can leave orphan after concurrent soft-delete; deleted members excluded from count but retain FK may block deletion; address overwrite deliberate bulk action
decision: Preserve workflow; transaction locks and household-person ownership constraints; simplify address duplication only if override/propagate semantics preserved.
behavior: Create copies person address when requested and installs head; joining copies household address only if person lacks meaningful address; leaving preserves address. Propagate intentionally overwrites all active members’ address and returns count. UI/actions log lifecycle changes.
acceptance: Concurrent create/delete/join produce no orphan or cross-plant grouping; inactive member retention handled explicitly; propagate preview/confirm shows affected people; leaving does not erase address.

title: Church-defined tags and person assignment
permissions: Owner/Admin manage and assign; plant readers
states: tag exists→renamed/recolored/deleted; link absent↔present
validation: Name max100 trim; named/hex colors; own tag/person; unique pair
failures: Repeated assign conflict no-op still writes tag_added activity; repeated removal may log nonexistent link; DB tag name not unique; nullable color DTO mismatch potential
decision: Keep tenant tag system; unique normalized-name decision explicit, no needless generic classification engine.
behavior: Tags are tenant-defined labels, not global canonical taxonomy; junction carries church_id and unique person+tag. Delete cascades links; separate use check powers deliberate UI.
acceptance: Foreign tag/person cannot link; retry logs one semantic assignment/removal; rename updates all views/export; deletion explains affected count and preserves audit facts.

title: Skills, gifts, proficiency and category grouping
permissions: Plant readers; Owner/Admin writes
states: skill added/updated/removed; optional proficiency
validation: Categories worship/tech/admin/teaching/hospitality/leadership/other; beginner/intermediate/advanced/expert; name1–100
failures: Skill mutation/history separate; remove hard-deletes item; arbitrary notes/content length needs bounded contract
decision: Preserve flexible inventory; simple table/domain operations suffice.
behavior: Skills inventory is practical contact data alongside SME interview gifted criterion; it does not replace that criterion or infer calling/fit. Category grouping done server-side.
acceptance: All enums/null clears/grouping and foreign IDs; revisions visible; skill removal does not rewrite qualification record; Evry may search recorded skills but never judge calling.

title: SME 4 C’s assessment recording, latest result and history
permissions: Plant readers; Owner/Admin human assessors; coach promised scope partial IDN-025
states: append new dated assessment; latest by assessmentDate then createdAt; no stage change
validation: Committed/Compelled/Contagious/Courageous each integer1–5; total recomputed4–20; date valid
failures: No DB score/sum constraints; JS Date→UTC day; separate insert/activity failure; equal-time latest needs tie-break
decision: Keep methodology unchanged; version canonical rubric labels and preserve date-only values. Atomic assessment+audit, typed qualification domain.
behavior: These four lenses are authoritative product methodology. This is a human-recorded person assessment, distinct from automated church Plant Intelligence rubric. Warning for earlier-than-Core Group is advisory, never a hard gate. Alpha correction preserves same lenses.
acceptance: All four notes/scores/date/history survive; total cannot be supplied forged; out-of-order historical dates show correct latest; human authorship recorded; no AI substitutes pastoral/person qualification judgment.

title: SME five-criterion interview, result, next steps and progression
permissions: Owner/Admin records human interview; reads same scope as qualification
states: append interview then status interviewed ANY result; history latest by interviewDate/createdAt
validation: Maturity/Gifted/Chemistry/Right Reasons/Season each pass/fail/concern; qualified/qualified_with_notes/not_qualified/follow_up; dated notes/nextSteps
failures: Unconditional status update can regress core_group/launch_team/leader; record may commit before status/history failure; FRD suggests task creation prompt not found in action
decision: Preserve methodology/result meaning. Decision required on repeat-record stage regression and optional next-step-task UX.
behavior: interviewed means interview happened, not qualified. FRD explicitly ANY result (:650,874). Criteria/result remain human judgment. Skipping prior stages is allowed with guidance. Main action sets interviewed irrespective current status, while FRD depicts forward event progression; regression needs explicit decision.
acceptance: All criteria and results preserved; any result records interviewed evidence; advanced-person repeat interview does not silently regress without approved rule; next-step task suggestion must be tracked as partial requirement, not invented implemented automation.

title: Commitment recording, private document and Core Group entry
permissions: Owner/Admin creates; same-plant readers download; witnessedBy supplied optional user UUID
states: dated core_group/launch_team record→person core_group; history append; document optional
validation: Core-group/launch-team type; valid signed date; optional witness;PDF/JPG/PNG max10 MiB
failures: 10 MiB promised commitment action exceeds v2 serverless request body cap noted by photo policy; upload may orphan on insert failure; witness UUID not shown to be same-plant; signed URL bearer1h
decision: Preserve authoritative commitment→Core Group semantics; fix file transport and history atomicity; treat type-versus-current-stage question explicitly.
behavior: Signing is Core Group entry per Playbook/FRD; no committed status. Both commitment types currently set core_group; advanced repeat-record can regress. document_url stores private key, unlike name. Document download uses signed URL rather than photo proxy.
acceptance: Private upload/download checked across plant/coach contexts; platform supports advertised10 MiB or uses approved direct-upload flow; same-plant witness or explicitly external witness model; record/status/audit atomic; repeat record follows approved regression rule.

title: Alpha corrections of assessment, interview and commitment records
permissions: Owner/Admin correct live own-plant person records; history private
states: before snapshot→corrected row+after snapshot; stale version→reload refusal
validation: Record/person UUID; closed kind;32-hex md5 version; original domain schema; assessment total recompute
failures: No document/witness/assessor replacement correction fields; no status re-advancement on correction; version hash depends raw JSON representation; entityId polymorphic without FK
decision: Include full target and qualification slice; prefer explicit row revision numbers and domain-owned revision history over hash-specific architecture. Decide correction reason/undo policy.
behavior: Alpha2107df58 only; one SQL locked CTE compares original row version, updates allowed fields and appends before/after/actor audit atomically. Corrections do not rewrite actor/date provenance columns or replay stage effects. No reversal/undo tool implemented.
acceptance: Stale/cross-person/cross-plant correction refused; total recomputed; history ordered with actor/time; correcting interview result or commitment date does not rerun recruitment automation; append duplicate submission safely or reject replay.

title: Duplicate hints and duplicate-pair review directory
permissions: Own-plant readers; merge Owner/Admin
states: exact/potential/no-match; hints never force merge
validation: Normalized email/phone/name; literal wildcard escaping; blank/short contact ignores; soft-deleted omitted
failures: Shared address/family names can be false positives; no universal unique email for contacts; detection does not prove same human
decision: Preserve human review; no AI automatic identity merge. Data quality hints remain advisory.
behavior: Duplicate checker returns current active candidate set and redacts import hints to ID/display name. Duplicate directory provides review rather than destructive deduplication.
acceptance: Blank/short/wildcard inputs, same name family, email casing and phone forms match documented predicates; no foreign contact exposed; user can intentionally create duplicate.

title: Field-choice duplicate merge, blockers, reference transfer, receipt and redirects
permissions: Owner/Admin; account-linked profile must survive; two linked profiles cannot merge
states: review→versioned locked merge→source soft-retired/survivor; repeat same source/survivor success
validation: Distinct active own-plant profiles; all differing fields choose stored left/right; no userId/storage arbitrary inputs; ownership consistency
failures: Block same-meeting attendance/response, training collision, live same-date follow-up, pending RSVP, self-referral and leadership authority change. Stale review refused; no automatic undo.
decision: Preserve reconciliation; reviewed destructive write default for Evry, human field choice. Own transaction with relation registry/schema coverage, explicit reversal design rather than naive undo.
behavior: Transfers19 FK/polymorphic references; shared tags deduped; source retained; survivorBefore and choices private receipt. Recursive redirect follows merge chains with cycle guard. Receipt unique source provides retry convergence. Photo choices operate on stored keys. Merge scope must incorporate alpha correction references/history policy; new v3 relation cannot be forgotten.
acceptance: Every relation transfer/collision tested on disposable DB; repeated command and stale version safe; no authority gained by merge; source docs/receipts retained; chain redirects stable; correction history remains discoverable for transferred person records.

title: CSV template, preview, row validation, duplicate resolutions and partial import
permissions: Owner/Admin imports; all plant seats download blank template
states: file→valid/invalid/duplicate rows→skip/create/review→created/skipped/errors+reviewPairs
validation: Required names/email/source; defaults prospect; resolutions closed enum; reparse client-returned raw rows
failures: Main line-split breaks quoted multiline; alpha BOM/quoted multiline/CRLF+malformed quote handling. No server file-size/row-count guard shown; no import-run receipt; replay duplicates partial successes; preview checks existing DB not intra-file duplicates
decision: Preserve contact import as new-customer workflow, unrelated to v2 customer migration. Choose proven CSV library or pure parser with tests; add run/row receipts if partial resumability retained.
behavior: Bulk import creates sequentially, counts per-row errors, allows intentional create or create-and-review, never overwrites matched contact. Review inserts new row then returns pair. Import accepts12 contact columns; it ignores exported status/tags/createdAt, so not lossless roundtrip.
acceptance: Alpha parser acceptance includes commas/escaped quotes/multiline/BOM/bad quoting. Invalid/duplicate choices preserve user intent; server caps bytes/rows; resumable import-run row idempotency prevents duplicate successful rows on retry; report error reasons, not counts only.

title: Filtered CSV export and file serialization
permissions: Plant seated read permission; oversight no raw export; coach export not implemented surface
states: filtered set→header+rows; empty→header-only
validation: Same list filters; CSV RFC4180 escaping; no server parse of arbitrary filter UUIDs shown
failures: All rows in memory; no formula-injection neutralization; status/tags/date export cannot roundtrip through narrower importer
decision: Keep full export. Decide formula-neutralization and lossless roundtrip requirements explicitly; never advertise existing import/export as a backup.
behavior: Export15 columns with tags semicolon-joined and UTCcreatedAt, notes/contact/address/status/source. Filenames people-export-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Photo/userId/private keys never exported.
acceptance: Filter equivalence including tags, empty export, comma/newline/quotes and formula-like content. Permission prevents org/foreign export; large export bounded/streamed; document deliberate formula-safe format tradeoff.

title: Recorded events and cross-domain recruitment auto-advancement
permissions: Domain operation actor should retain authenticated performer; current event helper uses original createdBy
states: vision attendance prospect→attendee; team membership core_group→launch_team; leadership launch_team→leader only
validation: Expected prior status; active own-plant person; out-of-order effects soft constrained
failures: Auto-advance catches/logs failure after original action; attribution uses person.createdBy instead of current performer; process-local event delivery not durable
decision: Keep domain outcomes; use direct in-transaction calls for critical changes and durable job/outbox only for external/asynchronous effects. Do not preserve generic event bus for its own sake.
behavior: Concrete callbacks only advance from designated prior state and do not regress advanced contacts. This differs from interview/commitment unconditional actions. Events are implementation plumbing, not permission authority or pastoral judgment.
acceptance: Each integration’s committed action/status/audit visible despite retry/crash; exact prior-status behavior preserved per approved methodology; authenticated actor retained; no event failure silently loses critical follow-up/assessment dirtying.

title: Person teams, training and communication tabs
permissions: Own-plant readers; compose control uses communication.send, not people.write
states: team memberships/training list; sent/delivered/opened/clicked/bounced/failed versus logged contact
validation: Same person/plant; date display intentional church zone
failures: Logged contact recipient status sent must not claim email delivery; empty history explanatory; profile wrapper controls missing/merged person
decision: Preserve tabs and cross-domain read DTOs; keep writes in owning domain operations; no duplicate person-specific send engine.
behavior: Person-centric operational history joins modules rather than only profile fields. Training date/status and team assignments visible. Communication tab distinguishes actual delivery from logged contact and hides send control for read-only account. Domain operation ownership remains Teams/Communication.
acceptance: Per-person lists match owning modules; logged contact badge never says delivered email; foreign/deleted/merged person behavior consistent; no widened permission by cross-module tab.

title: Deferred follow-up initiation handler and incomplete task suggestions
permissions: No functioning public follow-up handler grant
states: no-op warning; FRD task suggestions not implemented by qualification action
validation: No active subscriber
integrations: Tasks follow-up domain owns actual workflows
failures: Function logs DEFERRED; do not count it as implemented status/task automation
decision: Replace no-op; preserve real follow-up capabilities through Tasks inventory, mark suggestion requirement for decision.
behavior: Static source has exported handleFollowUpInitiated warning only. Following-up status is available manually and actual follow-up assignment exists in Tasks owner scope. FRD interview next-step creation suggestions are intended UX, not proven delivered here.
acceptance: Full target includes actual Tasks follow-up operations and explicit decision on qualification-driven suggestions; no no-op tool registered to Evry.

title: Unused pipeline conversion analytics service and component
permissions: Internal church-scoped read; no reachable route/action found
states: statusCounts and four forward-conversion pairs computed; no mounted UI
validation: Optional activity date range; ordered known statuses; same church
failures: Historical repeat transitions can count same person multiple times; current source-stage population mixed with event-window denominator; account-linked people included; all activity metadata loaded in memory
decision: Explicit product decision: implement transparent cohort-aware analytics if required, or retire unused internal artifact while preserving active Phase Intelligence metrics; do not claim delivered UI.
behavior: Static search found getPipelineMetrics only its definition and explanatory comment, and PipelineMetrics only its own component. No caller/import mounts this analytics. It counts active status population, then forward status_changed events, then computes exact adjacent transitions divided by current source-stage count plus all moves forward from that stage. Optional dates filter events but not population. This is a historical implemented helper/component, distinct from actual Phase Intelligence conversion calculations.
acceptance: Decision records whether to expose analytics. If activated, rates have explicit cohort/window/unit definition, exclude repeat moves and inappropriate staff attribution, handle zero evidence and match tested examples. No false claim of deployed conversion UI.
